title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not a Grothendieck manuscript. It is a typed, mimeographed page (p. 76, labelled 'n° 382') of what is almost certainly a Bourbaki redaction (draft) on manifolds and vector bundles, apparently reused as scrap paper. The neighbouring handwritten pages, on Lubin–Tate groups, Dieudonné modules and the filtrations M_K, t_G, ω_G, are presumably on other sheets or on the reverse. The handwritten '48' in the margin is the archive foliation.

Content, in modern terms:
(1) The page ends a list of identities for the exterior algebra bundle Λ(E) of a vector bundle E. These say that wedge product and interior product i(s) are bilinear over the ring of functions: (fω)∧ω' = f(ω∧ω') = ω∧(fω') and i(fs)ω = f·i(s)ω = i(s)(fω).
(2) 6.8.10 defines the k-th symmetric power bundle S^k(E), whose fibres are S^k(E_x). The analogous statements are left to the reader.
(3) 6.9 'Changement de structure': a C^r vector bundle is also C^{r'} for r' ≤ r, and also a topological vector bundle. A bundle that is analytic over an extension of K (e.g. C over R) is also analytic over K.
(4) 6.9.2: these forgetful functors commute with pullbacks and with the gluing construction of bundles from cocycles (n° 6.6).

This matches the style and content of Bourbaki, Variétés différentielles et analytiques, Fascicule de résultats (§7, fibrés vectoriels), though the draft numbering differs.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typed Bourbaki draft page with entirely standard material on vector bundles, reused as scrap paper. It has no connection to Grothendieck's handwritten crystalline/Lubin–Tate notes on the neighbouring pages and contains nothing original.
transcription_corrections: The page is typewritten (Bourbaki draft, n° 382, p. 76), not handwritten. The only handwriting is the archive number '48' in the lower-left margin.
In 6.8.10 the phrases 'puissance symétrique' and 'k-ième' are underlined, as is the section title 'Changement de structure' in 6.9.
In the first line the multiplication is written 'f.(ω∧ω′)' with a typewriter point; the primes on ω are typed as small superscript marks.
